Ruling

Partial refund PARTIAL_REFUND

The judge's explanation, as written

To the rider and the driver. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. The trip and the measurement. TRP-02839 was driven on 21 August 2026. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02839 measures 24.6 km against the booked optimal of 20.0 km on trip record EV-TRIP-02839, an excess of 4.6 km and 23% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation is established, and the trace figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy. The trace itself is sound: 193 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), and the escalation triggers in POL-RD-10(2), (3), (4), (5) and (8) are not engaged. The rider needed no extra corroboration under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d is 0), and the burden that shifted to the driver was discharged by a specific artifact and clause, not a general assertion. The extra distance is excused. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02839-01 is on file and admissible at full weight: a HIGH-severity CLOSURE on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway towards ECP after Defu Flyover, active 17:53:08 to 19:20:08, which wholly covers the trip window of 18:23:08 to 18:55:08, with the platform recording that it intersects the route and overlaps the trip window, and a shortest lawful alternative of 23.0 km. The trace records zero fixes inside the closed segment's area, with a closest approach of 1,350.67 m - the closest test of POL-RD-03 limb (c) this record allows, and consistent with a route that leaves the corridor before the affected segment. The two submissions on limb (c) are answered together: the rider says it cannot be verified because the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record, the driver says the trace proves the diversion. On this record the advisory's own route-intersection fact plus the trace's avoidance of the closed area is the best evidence there is, and it supports exoneration. (If a party wishes to contest limb (c), the optimal route's polyline is the item that would settle it - that is the one open question in this case, and it does not need a referral.) POL-RD-03's cap is 1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km, which exceeds the 4.6 km measured, so the whole excess is justified and the deviation is fully excused. What follows. Because an exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation, POL-RD-02 does not run at all - its own terms apply only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation. That disposes of both competing figures: the rider's $7.85 recomputation against the booked optimal route (35.01 - 27.16) and the driver's $2.70 recomputation against the closure-adjusted route (35.01 - 32.35) both fail, because no POL-RD-02 recomputation issues. The distance and time charges stand. What is refunded. The one charge the rider recovers is the ERP line, ECP Fort Rd eastbound, $3.00 (EV-FARE-02839). It is off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false; optimal-route ERP $0.00). The crossing is genuine, not phantom: the nearest driver fix to the gantry is 59.12 m at 18:39:08, inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets, so the rider's 'a gantry I would never have passed' does not make out a billing-integrity failure, there is no POL-RD-09(4) referral, and no full refund follows on that theory. But the rider did not cause the closure either, so under POL-RD-09(2) that $3.00 is refunded as a standalone pass-through correction (the SGD 12.00 cap is not reached). Charged total $35.01; refund $3.00; the rider pays $32.01. The driver's submission that NO_ACTION would leave the present state standing is right as a description of POL-GEN-03, but the off-route ERP line is refundable, so the outcome is a partial refund of $3.00 rather than no action. Referrals and compensation. No referral issues. POL-RD-06 does not fire: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 197 completed trips in 90 days (about 0.005), below both the 3-flag and the 0.05 tests, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no driver-conduct review, and no uplift - the deviation is not MATERIAL in any event (23% against 50%, 4.6 km against 8.0 km, and nil on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment). No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed the full 24.6 km the trace records, so there is no unbilled distance under POL-RD-04. Profile fields. rating, lifetime counters and cancellation rates on either profile are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used to decide anything about this trip; the rider's mention of them was flagged by the referee and is correct as far as it goes. Execution. The monetary effect is $3.00, below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it is released on issue. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal), and POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km — not the rounded trip_record copy — the governing field. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

evidence EV-GPS-02839, EV-TRIP-02839 · clauses POL-RD-01, POL-RD-08

kept Nothing here needs corroboration from outside the trace: 193 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds mean the trace satisfies none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c), so the deviation may be established on the trace alone and no independent source is required.

evidence EV-GPS-02839 · clauses POL-RD-07, POL-RD-08

kept The rider's own record raises no extra hurdle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the condition in POL-RD-08 for corroboration beyond the trace (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met, and no other field on either profile — rating, lifetime counters, cancellation rate — may be used to decide this trip under POL-GEN-01.

evidence EV-RPROF-02839 · clauses POL-RD-08, POL-GEN-01

kept The driver's 'KPE closed, LTA advisory on file' answer is an exoneration only if POL-RD-03 limb (c) is met, that is, an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. The trace does not show it: 0 fixes fall inside the advisory's area and the vehicle's closest approach to it is 1350.67 m, and the optimal route's own polyline is absent from the record. A limb that cannot be verified on the admitted evidence does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08, and an unverified limb exonerates nothing.

evidence EV-ADVIS-02839-01, EV-GPS-02839 · clauses POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08

kept If the closure does not exonerate, the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it runs on the booked optimal route under POL-RD-02: charged_total is $35.01; the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 20.0 + 0.28 x 27.0) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown) + $0.80 platform fee + $0.00 ERP on the optimal route = $27.16; the refund is therefore $35.01 - $27.16 = $7.85. That is above the $0.50 de minimis floor and is only 22.4% of charged_total, far short of the 90% at which a full refund would issue, so the rider asks for PARTIAL_REFUND of the $7.00 he contested.

evidence EV-FARE-02839, EV-TRIP-02839, EV-GPS-02839 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-01

kept The $3.00 ECP Fort Rd eastbound line is a crossing the booked route never makes: fare_breakdown records on_optimal_route false for that gantry and optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00, so the optimal-route recomputation carries no ERP at all. The trace's nearest fix to the gantry is 59.1 m at 18:39:08, so under POL-RD-09's 250 m match rule the crossing is real and the line is not a phantom charge — but it is a gantry the rider did not ask to cross. If the closure exoneration is found instead of a deviation, POL-RD-09(2) still refunds that off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00, because the rider did not cause the closure either; and since the justified excess (4.6 km) equals the measured excess (4.6 km), no excess remains to be refunded under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route.

evidence EV-FARE-02839, EV-TRIP-02839, EV-GPS-02839 · clauses POL-RD-09, POL-RD-03

kept On the primary route the $3.00 is inside the $7.85 and must not be added to it: POL-RD-09(1) provides that where a deviation is refunded under POL-RD-02, off-route ERP is already comprehended in that refund, because the recomputed fare carries only on-optimal-route gantries and here carries $0.00 of ERP. The rider claims the comprehended figure, not a doubled one.

evidence EV-FARE-02839 · clauses POL-RD-09, POL-RD-02

evidence EV-FARE-02839, EV-GPS-02839 · clauses POL-RD-09

evidence EV-GPS-02839, EV-TRIP-02839, EV-FARE-02839, EV-ADVIS-02839-01 · clauses POL-RD-10, POL-RD-07

The trace itself is sound: 193 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), and the escalation triggers in POL-RD-10(2), (3), (4), (5) and (8) are not engaged. The rider needed no extra corroboration under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d is 0), and the burden that shifted to the driver was discharged by a specific artifact and clause, not a general assertion. For both of you: this ruling refunds $3.00 of the $7.00 the rider contested. Facts not in dispute. The trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip TRP-02839, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure — 24.6 km — the governing distance, not the rounded trip-record copy. Against a booked optimal of 20.0 km that is an excess of 4.6 km, 23.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so a deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, and the trace is unimpaired (193 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s), so it stands on the trace alone. The deviation is NOT material: 4.6 km is below the 8.0 km threshold and 23.0% is below the 50% threshold, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 197, far short of the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern, so there is no uplift to FULL_REFUND and no driver-conduct referral. The rider's own profile raises no extra corroboration hurdle (deviation_claims_60d is 0), and no profile field has been used as a ground of decision about this trip (POL-GEN-01). The driver's closure excuse succeeds. EV-ADVIS-02839-01 is an LTA advisory on file: a HIGH-severity closure on the KPE towards ECP after Defu Flyover, active 17:53:08 to 19:20:08, wholly covering the trace window of 18:23:08 to 18:55:08. The platform records it as intersecting the optimal route — limb (a) — and its window covers the time the vehicle would have reached the segment, with the 15-minute buffer — limb (b). For limb (c), the record does not carry the optimal route's own polyline, so the closest test the record allows is the trace's relationship to the advisory area: 0 of 193 fixes fall inside it and the closest approach is 1350.67 m, meaning the vehicle never entered the closed segment; with a driven distance of 24.6 km against a 23.0 km shortest lawful alternative, and the vehicle crossing an off-optimal gantry at 18:39, that supports the diversion the driver describes. I therefore find limb (c) met and reject the rider's argument that the limb cannot be verified. The exoneration is capped at min(4.60 km, 1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km) = 4.60 km, so the whole excess is excused and nothing remains to refund under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 24.6 km. What that means for the money. The distance and time charges stand (POL-RD-09(2) — the driver is not at fault for the closure). Charged_total was $35.01; the recomputed fare is $27.16 on the booked optimal and $32.3460 on the closure-adjusted optimal, but no POL-RD-02 refund runs once the excess is fully exonerated, so the rider's $7.85 figure is not payable — as the rider's own alternative case concedes. The line that IS refunded is the ERP. The ECP Fort Rd eastbound charge of $3.00 is off the optimal route (optimal_route_erp_sgd $0.00; off_optimal_route_total $3.00), and the trace passes within 59.12 m of the gantry (fix 96, 18:39:08), inside POL-RD-09's 250 m match radius, so the crossing is real and the line is not a phantom charge — no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral. But the rider did not cause the closure either, so under POL-RD-09(2) that $3.00 is refunded as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00. The driver's submission that $2.70 is the rider's ceiling, and that the $3.00 is already comprehended and must not be added, is rejected: the POL-RD-09(1) comprehension rule applies only where a POL-RD-02 refund actually runs, and here it does not. No escalation. The trace meets none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs; the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the advisory invoked is present and covers the trip window; every charge line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record; and there is no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength. POL-RD-10 is not engaged on any limb. Outcome. $3.00 is returned to the rider (the off-route ERP pass-through); the rest of the $35.01 fare stands. That monetary effect is below the $8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically (POL-GEN-05). Confidence is 0.82; every artifact this ruling rests on — EV-GPS-02839, EV-TRIP-02839, EV-FARE-02839 and EV-ADVIS-02839-01 — carries weight 1.0, so no discount applies and the escalation floor is not approached.
